one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings in the window (FQ1 FY27 report expected mid/late December). The print on 30 Sep beat and guided FQ1 ~8% above consensus, yet the stock closed only +0.9% vs the pre-print close by 2 Oct, so post-earnings drift looks muted rather than a strong tailwind. Events inside 5 Oct-1 Nov: (1) Micron Taiwan Taoyuan union strike-authorization vote closes 6 Oct, Micron board proposal due ~8 Oct, Taichung mediation 22 Oct [8,9,10]; authorization is likely (80%+ backed it in August) but an actual walkout is less likely and Taoyuan is ~2,800 staff, so this is a headline/negative-skew risk more than a supply event; a concession toward 15% profit sharing would hit FY27 EPS sentiment. (2) Korean peers' Q3 results (Samsung prelim early Oct, SK hynix late Oct) and hyperscaler capex updates in late October (judgment on timing): read-through on AI capex and HBM; given TrendForce's 4Q26 contract increases [3] and spot still near highs [4], I expect neutral-to-supportive. (3) Spot DDR5 momentum is decelerating (30d +3.7% vs +6.7% a week earlier) [4], a watch item. Net: near-symmetric lognormal around spot with monthly sigma ~20% (a bit below 80%/3.5=23% since realized vol is inflated by the 490% run), tiny positive drift, P(>=spot) ~0.475.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of (a) FY28 EPS $195 x 5.5x = $1,073 and (b) normalized EPS $110 x 9.5x = $1,045 plus ~$120/sh projected net cash = $1,165.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 (Aug-28) EPS $195 x 5.5x forward P/E (value in Oct 2027 when FY28 is the forward year)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus $205.95 [11] cut ~5%: management guides 'more moderate' price increases through FY27 and higher opex (+$2.5B) [2]; TrendForce 4Q26 conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ is a deceleration from prior quarters [3]; Taiwan union push for 15% of operating profit (vs current one-off bonuses) raises labour-cost risk [8].

Memory-maker peers (SK hynix 4.49x, Samsung 4.46x, Nanya 4.92x, Kioxia 4.31x, Winbond 4.24x, Macronix 3.97x, Phison 5.30x, SanDisk 8.04x) cluster at 4-5x forward [12]; MU trades 6.1x FY27 / 5.2x FY28 consensus [11,12]. 5.5x sits inside the peer range, modestly above the memory median for MU's US listing, $68B net cash and capital-return policy, below today's FY27 multiple because by Oct 2027 the market will be pricing the 2028 capacity wave.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Through-cycle (normalized) EPS $110 x 9.5x = $1,045, plus projected net cash ~$120/share at Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus GM path declines from ~84% to ~65% by FY2030 [10]; on ~$250B revenue (below FY27 consensus $274.9B [11]) at ~55% operating margin and 15.5% tax [2] gives ~$116B NI / ~1.13B shares = ~$103; nudged to $110 because 26 SCAs (>35% of revenue to 2030, ~$150B RPO at floor prices with margins 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak') [2] lift the trough. Prior-cycle margin collapse from low-60s to 27% [7] is the cautionary history.

On normalized (not peak) earnings memory names have traded ~10-13x forward when earnings were mid-cycle [7]; 9.5x is inside the 11-peer forward P/E range 3.97-23.73x [12] and below the HDD/controller names that carry structurally lower capital intensity.

Net cash $68.3B and $12.7B customer deposits (liability) at FQ4 [2]; FY26 adjusted FCF $62.3B [1]; FY27 OCF ~$190B less capex >$50B (FQ1 $11.5B, 1H $25B, 2H higher) [2] less ~$50B returns gives ~$150B net cash, minus deposits ~$137B, ~1.13B shares, rounded down to $120 for execution risk.

bear.story: Spot DDR5 rolls over in 1H27 as consumer demand destruction (PC units down double digits) meets HBM pricing reset; investors look through 2027 to the simultaneous 2028 capacity wave (Micron ID1/ID2, Japan, Samsung P5, Hynix new fabs) and an AI capex pause; FY28 EPS cut to ~$150 and multiple compresses to ~3.5-4x plus cash.

base.story: FY27 delivers ~$175-185 EPS with sequential growth as guided; pricing moderates but supply stays tight into 2028; Taiwan labour dispute settles with higher but bounded profit sharing; market pays ~5.5x FY28 EPS ~$195 plus growing cash and buybacks from Dec 2026.

bull.story: Shortage deepens in 2027-28 (SemiAnalysis-style undersupply widening, HBM ASP +121% in 2027), SCAs/RPO convince investors earnings are durable, FY28 EPS ~$230 and multiple re-rates toward 7-8x with large capital return.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 3.97x (Macronix) to 23.73x (Seagate); memory-maker subset (7 names) 3.97-8.04x, median 4.46x. EV/EBITDA median and range are TRAILING (7.01x Samsung to 43.37x Seagate) because forward EBITDA was not available (Twelve Data statistics needs a paid plan; Alpha Vantage rate-limited).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.5x forward on FY28 EPS: above the memory-maker median (4.46x) and all-peer median (4.92x), well inside the 3.97-23.73x range; below MU's current 6.1x FY27.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Small premium to Korean/Taiwanese memory makers only: persistent structural factors are (1) net cash of $68.3B and a stated plan to return 100% of excess cash from Dec 2026 [2] vs peers with lower payout, (2) Korean-listing discount affecting Samsung/SK hynix, (3) SCA contracts covering >35% of revenue to 2030 with floor-price bands [2]. Not using any sell-side outperformance call. HDD and controller peers (WDC, STX, SIMO) trade far higher due to lower capital intensity; I do not apply their multiples.

thesis_break_reason: $700 is ~3.4x FY28 consensus EPS and roughly 3x after netting ~$120/sh cash: at that level the market would be pricing a halving of FY28 earnings, i.e. DRAM contract prices turning down well before the 2028 capacity additions or an AI capex cut. That would contradict management's 'no line of sight to balance' and the SCA/RPO floors, so it would most likely mean a real cycle turn rather than volatility (an 80%-vol stock can drop 20-25% on noise, which only reaches ~$820-860).

key_uncertainties: Timing of the memory price peak: spot DDR5 still at cycle highs but 30-day momentum halving; contract increases decelerating from earlier 2026 quarters.
2028 capacity wave (Micron, Samsung P5, SK hynix new fabs) and how early the market discounts it.
Labour cost structure: Taiwan union demand for 15% of operating profit (~$15B on FY26) could set a precedent beyond Taiwan.
Micron's HBM4 share at Nvidia appears supplementary vs SK hynix 60-70% and Samsung 25-30%; custom HBM4E (NVHBM) is the offset.

Macro/AI capex: recession and AI-bubble prediction markets are liquid (Kalshi 2027 recession market ~$0.6M volume) but current probabilities could not be read reliably (pages blocked/conflicting snippets), so not used numerically.
Consensus FY27/FY28 EPS still moving after the print (Yahoo $176 vs MarketBeat quarterly sum ~$189).
reasoning: Facts: FQ4 FY26 revenue $54.2B, non-GAAP EPS $33.42, FQ1 FY27 guide $61.5B / $38.15 (~8% above consensus), net cash $68.3B, 26 SCAs with ~$150B RPO, capex >$50B in FY27 [1,2]. Alternative-lane checks: (a) pricing trackers say the cycle is still up but decelerating: TrendForce 4Q26 conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ, NAND +15-20%, 2027 HBM ASP +121% [3]; DDR5 die spot $57.33, +3.7% 30d (was +6.7%) and 'demand selective' near cycle high [4]; Amazon retail DDR5 $18.48/GB, +8.6% m/m, 100th percentile of 52w range [5]; consumer demand destruction is visible (PC units falling). (b) Independent writers: NewMaxx argues HBM pivot keeps conventional DRAM scarce into 2027 [6]; LongYield frames MU as a high-quality cyclical earning far above mid-cycle, with capex the classic top signal [7]. (c) Unpriced-ish risk: Taiwan union strike vote 1-6 Oct and 15% profit-share demand, confirmed by two independent sources [8,9] plus [10]. (d) Hiring: observed headcount only +3.7% y/y [14], i.e. Micron is not yet in a hiring-led capacity splurge, though capex is rising. Reddit and X could not be fetched (blocked), Benzinga and Digitimes returned 403; Twelve Data statistics required a paid plan and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so peer data came from stockanalysis pages [12]. Valuation: peers at ~4-5x forward show the market already treats memory earnings as peak; I value MU at 5.5x FY28 EPS $195 ($1,073) and on normalized EPS $110 x 9.5x + $120 cash ($1,165), blend $1,119 (+4%). Scenarios bear $620 (25%) / base $1,150 (50%) / bull $1,750 (25%), mean ~$1,167. Ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.32 bear, 0.24 base/bull), giving median ~$1,140 and an effective spread consistent with ~60-65% annual vol, below the 80% realized because realized is inflated by the one-way 490% run; tails kept fat (P>=$430 0.965, P>=$2,687 0.015). Thesis break $700. One-month: no company event; strike headlines and peer/hyperscaler prints are the window's events; near-symmetric at ~20% monthly sigma.
